main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snow roof slope seen from above (rows 8-35) over a front wall with a plank door and two shuttered windows (rows 36-62)
top_band: Snow roof slope, pale blue-white (L 166-249), rows 8-34 at x=32, with a darker snow edge at rows 33-35 and icicles
evidence: The column at x=32 runs from the outline at row 7 through the snow roof, which is a tall, textured slope in light tones (rows 8-34). The darker blue snow lip at rows 34-35 marks the front edge. Directly below, rows 37-38 (L=30) are a dark eave shadow under the overhang. Below that comes the front wall in brown wood tones (rows 39-62), with the door set between posts and the windows inset behind shutters. This matches the reference houses, where a roof slope sits above a wall face. Both the roof surface and the front face are clearly drawn, so it is a correct 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The snow ramp has about 5 steps (#f6f9fd, #dce5f1, #bccade, #97a8c6, #7383a8) with clumpy, per-patch variation. Outlines are tinted: dark brown beside wood and dark navy beside snow, with 0% neutral dark edge pixels. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Colours per tile are 17, against 18 and 11 for the references, so the tiles are about as rich. Total distinct colours (37) are fewer than the references (185 and 66), but the piece is small and uses a locked cool palette. Wood grain, glowing windows, icicles and a metal-banded door give it detail comparable to the references.
